images.caption: Formal portrait of Thomas Condon (1822–1907), a minister and geologist who gained recognition for his work in paleontology. He is especially known for his work with fossils in what became John Day Fossil Beds National Monument in the U.S. state of Oregon.

images.filename: Belly of the Whale (9939833084).jpg
images.caption: The spine of the whale is a small fault which has allowed a trickle of water through. Over time, the water enlarged a space which it eagerly filled, and as time went on, the water dug deeper, leaving rib-like ridges in the wall, called rills.
images.alt: The spine of the whale is a small fault which has allowed a trickle of water through. Over time, the water enlarged a space which it eagerly filled, and as time went on, the water dug deeper, leaving rib-like ridges in the wall, called rills.
images.artist: Oregon Caves from Cave Junction, USA

images.filename: Miller's Chapel (9939448605).jpg
images.caption: Miller's Chapel exhibits some of the cave's largest formations. Central to this room are a column and a stalactite-stalagmite duo that may eventually join together if given enough time.
images.alt: Miller's Chapel exhibits some of the cave's largest formations. Central to this room are a column and a stalactite-stalagmite duo that may eventually join together if given enough time.

images.filename: Calcite Crystals (9939943773).jpg
images.caption: Carbonic acid which is carrying minerals in the air can grow crystals on rock faces in which it regularly condenses.

images.filename: Paradise Lost (9939473016).jpg
images.caption: Visitors to this room must crane their necks and watch their feet! The room is a speleogen called a domepit, where a cave waterfall has slowly carved out a massive vertical hole through the rock. As the water slows,  dozens of drapery formations grow down the side. The water which still comes through leaves a pool in the center of the room which visitors must step around.

images.filename: Compression Joints (9940653933).jpg
images.caption: As the rock undergoes stress due to the earth's shift, weaknesses can form, called joints. In this case, as the rock compressed, joints formed to relieve pressure.
images.alt: As the rock undergoes stress due to the earth's shift, weaknesses can form, called joints. In this case, as the rock compressed, joints formed to relieve pressure.
images.artist: Oregon Caves from Cave Junction, USA

images.caption: Bevels are ridges in the rock that run perpendicular to the direction of a passageway. They form as a result of an ancient river rushing through the passage, hurling all manner of sand and debris against the walls as it goes. As the name implies, these particles bevel out the walls.
images.alt: Bevels are ridges in the rock that run perpendicular to the direction of a passageway. They form as a result of an ancient river rushing through the passage, hurling all manner of sand and debris against the walls as it goes. As the name implies, these particles bevel out the walls.
images.artist: Oregon Caves from Cave Junction, USA

images.filename: Active Moonmilk (9940495425).jpg
images.caption: Moonmilk is an Actinomyces bacterial growth in the cave which in some strains may have properties similar to Penicillin. While much of it has dried and been encased in formation, active moonmilk still exists in this cave and others.
images.alt: Moonmilk is an Actinomyces bacterial growth in the cave which in some strains may have properties similar to Penicillin. While much of it has dried and been encased in formation, active moonmilk still exists in this cave and others.

images.filename: Dry Room Bedding Planes (9940663963).jpg
images.caption: This room features two massive slabs of marble, called beds, which have split and created a large crevice in the rock between the two.
